summary: How to ask happy customers to speak and to bring others, honestly: identify the moments when a customer has genuinely benefited, write the request that respects consent, frame questions that produce specific and usable answers, record permission before anything is used, and structure a referral proposal whose incentives and tracking are owner decisions; the method never drafts a testimonial, result or review on a customer's behalf.

requiredInputs.purpose: The owner's description of when customers first benefit, reach a milestone and complete the main journey.
How consent and permission are recorded by the platform or owner; the method never infers consent.
Approved offer facts for any referral proposal.
Owner limits on incentives (budget, legal, policy).

decisionSteps.instruction: From customerJourneyMoments choose up to three moments when a customer has verifiably benefited (first result, milestone, completion). For each, state the observable trigger the owner can see and why a request then is fair to the customer.

Write a short request and a standard request for each moment in the brand voice: why the brand is asking, what will be done with the answer, that it is optional, and how consent is recorded per consentProcess. Write one gentle follow-up for non-response. No incentive for a review unless incentiveConstraints allow it and the law of the owner's market permits it, in which case the owner decides.

Write two or three question sets of three to four questions each that invite specific, situational answers (what the situation was, what changed, what they would tell someone deciding) rather than ratings or praise.

Specify how a consented answer may be presented: quote with the attribution the customer approved, a short situation-to-result account in the customer's words, or a request to record a short video; each format states exactly what consent covers and that edits are limited to trimming.

Propose a referral structure as owner decisions: who the likely referrers are (from the brand profile), what is referred (usually the easiest first offer, from verified facts), incentive options with the constraints each depends on, and the tracking mechanism the platform actually provides or an owner-managed alternative. Draft the referral message in three lengths for the owner to approve.

Hand request drafts and messages to the existing approval and (where it exists) sending path; hand consented answers to the brand pack's proof section only through the consent record. No request is sent and no proof is used by this pack.

rules.instruction: The method writes requests and questions only. It never writes a testimonial, review, quote, result or case account for a customer to approve, and never paraphrases an answer into stronger claims.
rules.check: No customer-voice text appears except quoted consented answers.

rules.instruction: No answer, name, image, logo or result is used anywhere until consentProcess records permission for that exact use and attribution.
rules.appliesWhen: Any use of a customer contribution.
rules.check: Each usage references a consent record.

rules.instruction: Every request states that responding is optional and what the answer will be used for; it never implies an obligation, reciprocity or that others have already responded unless true and recorded.
rules.check: Request text contains the optional statement and the use statement.

rules.instruction: Incentive types, amounts and eligibility appear only as options with their constraints; the owner selects. Incentives for reviews are proposed only where incentiveConstraints and the applicable law allow, and the request discloses any incentive.
rules.check: Options labelled with constraints; disclosure present where an incentive is proposed.

rules.instruction: Tracking links, codes, forms or automated sends are described as proposals unless the runtime confirms the capability.

qualityChecks.criterion: Every usage format references the consent record it needs.
Incentives and tracking surfaced as owner decisions with constraints.

revisionPolicy.stopWhen: All checks pass or remaining items are owner decisions.

outputContract.customerFacing: Request drafts, question sets and referral messages in whatever existing draft format the runtime provides, for owner approval; nothing is sent or published by this pack.
outputContract.internalSidecar: Request moments, usage formats with consent requirements, referral proposal, owner decisions and findings.

examples.fictionalBrand: Fictional home-maintenance business (illustrative name: Bramble Home Care; every fact below is invented for illustration)
examples.inputScenario: Moments: first completed visit, six months on the plan, a resolved emergency. consentProcess: a reply confirming permission is stored by the owner. incentiveConstraints: no payment for reviews.
examples.expectedBehaviour: Three request moments with triggers; short and standard requests stating optionality and use; one follow-up; question sets about the situation before, what changed and what they would tell a neighbour; usage formats requiring a consent record per attribution; referral proposal naming plan members as likely referrers and a service credit option labelled as an owner decision; no review incentive proposed.
examples.forbiddenBehaviour: Drafting 'Bramble saved us hundreds' for the customer to sign, using an answer before consent is stored, or stating a referral code system exists.

examples.fictionalBrand: Fictional B2B scheduling business (illustrative name: Slotwise; every fact below is invented for illustration)
examples.inputScenario: Moments: calendar connected, first full month without a double booking, renewal. consentProcess: in-app consent form. incentiveConstraints: credit up to an illustrative cap.
examples.expectedBehaviour: Requests tied to the three moments with the in-app consent step; questions that elicit the manager's situation and what changed; referral proposal with credit options under the cap, tracking marked as owner-managed unless the runtime confirms links; three message lengths for approval.
examples.forbiddenBehaviour: Promising referrers an amount above the cap, implying other clinics already referred, or writing a case study from an unanswered request.

provenance.originalityNotes: Original design: the verifiable-benefit moment rule, consent-before-use and never-draft-the-customer rules, disclosure of incentives and the owner-decision structure for referral incentives were written for this platform. Asking for testimonials at good moments and structuring referral programmes is common practice; no third-party scripts, question banks, email templates or incentive menus were reused.
